insurer: Aditya Birla Health Insurance Co. Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (as per Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table)

great.name: Co-pay
great.quote: Co-payment means a cost sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the policyholder/insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.
great.explanation: Only a glossary definition of co-payment is provided and no clause is shown that actually applies a co-pay to your claims. This means no co-pay is charged and the insurer pays 100% of admissible claims, which is better than plans that impose 10–20% co-pay.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with Us.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for the first 36 months from the first policy start date. Claims for PEDs will be payable only after you complete 3 continuous years of coverage.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage, after the date of inception of the first policy with Us.
good.reference: Section D.I.2 (Specified disease / procedure waiting period)
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months from the first policy start date. You will need to complete 2 continuous years before these conditions become payable.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident, provided the same are covered.
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered in the first 30 days, but accidents are covered from day 1 (if covered otherwise). This is a standard initial waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: We shall cover the Medical Expenses incurred towards the Insured Person’s Domiciliary Hospitalization, up to the limits as specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy
good.explanation: Home-based hospitalization is covered up to the limits mentioned in the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table. This helps when treatment is medically required at home instead of in a hospital.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: Domestic Emergency Assistance Services (including Air Ambulance)
good.explanation: Domestic emergency assistance includes air ambulance as part of the assistance services. This can help arrange emergency medical transport, subject to the assistance terms and any limits in the policy documents.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Reasonable and Customary Charges for Room Rent for accommodation in Hospital room and other boarding charges up to the limits as specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy;
bad.reference: Section C.I.(a) In-patient Hospitalization – What is covered
bad.explanation: Room rent is payable only up to the limit mentioned in the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table, not at actuals. If the limit is low, it can restrict room choice and may also trigger proportionate deductions.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: If the Insured Person is admitted in a room category/limit that is higher than the one that is specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy, then the Insured Person shall bear a rateable proportion of the total Associated Medical Expenses
bad.explanation: If you choose a room category higher than your eligible limit, you must pay a proportionate share of the total associated medical expenses. This can significantly increase out-of-pocket costs beyond just the room rent difference.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Non-Medical Expenses including but not limited to ... as specified in the Annexure B - Non- Medical Expenses and on Our website
bad.reference: Specific Exclusions, point 50; Annexure B - List of Non-Medical Expenses
bad.explanation: Non-medical/consumable items listed in Annexure B are excluded from coverage. You will have to pay these common hospital charges (like gloves, masks, syringes, etc.) yourself.

unclear.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
unclear.quote: We shall cover on a reimbursement basis, up to the Sum Insured for the number of days as specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy, the Insured Person’s Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses
unclear.reference: Section C.I.(b) Pre – hospitalization Medical Expenses
unclear.explanation: Pre-hospitalization expenses are covered, but the number of days is only stated in the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table. The actual coverage window (e.g., 30/60/90 days) cannot be confirmed from this extract.

unclear.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
unclear.quote: We shall cover on a reimbursement basis, up to the Sum Insured for the number of days specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy, the Insured Person’s Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses
unclear.reference: Section C.I.(c) Post – hospitalization Medical Expenses
unclear.explanation: Post-hospitalization expenses are covered, but the number of days is only stated in the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table. The actual coverage window (e.g., 60/90/180 days) cannot be confirmed from this extract.

unclear.name: Deductible
unclear.quote: All claims under these Benefits will be payable only if the aggregate of covered Medical Expenses... in a Policy Year is in excess of the Deductible as stated in the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table of this Policy
unclear.reference: Section C.I (Basic Covers) – applicability of deductible
unclear.explanation: Claims are payable only after you cross a deductible amount in a policy year, as per the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table. Your out-of-pocket cost depends on the deductible value, which is not provided in this extract.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: Cashless Facilities can be availed only at Our Network Providers/ Empaneled Service Providers. The complete list of Network Providers and Empaneled Service Providers is available on Our website
unclear.explanation: Cashless treatment is available only at network/empanelled providers listed by the insurer. The network size (number of hospitals) is not stated here, so ease of finding a cashless hospital cannot be judged from this extract.

unclear.name: Restore Benefit
unclear.quote: The Sum Insured and/or the sub-limit for each Benefit under Section C.I is specified against that Benefit in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy.
unclear.reference: Section C (Benefits Covered Under the Policy) – introductory text
unclear.explanation: The extract does not state any restore/reinstatement of Sum Insured after a claim. Whether a restore benefit exists (and its rules) cannot be confirmed without the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table.

unclear.name: No Claim Bonus
unclear.quote: The Policy Schedule shall specify which of the following covers are in force and available for the Insured Persons under the Policy during the Policy Period.
unclear.explanation: The extract only says the Policy Schedule will specify which covers apply, but it does not confirm whether a No Claim Bonus/renewal bonus exists. Whether your Sum Insured increases on claim-free renewals cannot be determined from this extract.

unclear.name: Built-in SI Buffer
unclear.quote: The funds accumulated under HealthReturns TM may be utilized ... towards ... (i) In-patient Medical Expenses and Day Care Treatment, provided that the Sum Insured, is exhausted during the Policy Year.
unclear.reference: Section C.II.(l) HealthReturns™ – How can one spend HealthReturnsTM
unclear.explanation: HealthReturns™ funds can be used for in-patient and day care expenses after the Sum Insured is exhausted in the same policy year. It is not clear from this extract whether this works like an insurer-funded additional Sum Insured buffer or a customer-earned wallet with separate rules/limits.
